title: Dragon Tree: Ancient Dragon Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Cut the bark and the sap runs dark red, which is how it got the name. Six dragon trees mapped in Lisbon, Palermo and Cadiz.
intro: Nobody can date a dragon tree, and that is the species rather than sloppy record keeping. Dracaena draco lays down no annual rings, so every age here is an estimate and some are wide open: the tree in the Parque Genoves in Cadiz is put anywhere between 100 and 200 years. The name comes from the sap. Cut into the bark and the resin that runs out is dark red, sold across Europe for centuries as dragon's blood, a dye and a medicine. Shape is the other reason to go. An old dragon tree spreads into a low dome of blunt branch tips, and the one at the Quinta Conde dos Arcos in Lisbon is more than twice as wide as it is tall, a crown almost 14 metres across on a tree of 6.2 metres. Six are mapped, three of them in Lisbon and two in Palermo.
